Hi John / Sasha —

Thanks for taking the time today — appreciate the clear context on Acme's compliance checklist. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in scope for our hosted API (we maintain an external report; summary attached).
- Audit logging capabilities we discussed: admin activity logs (UI/admin actions), API request/response logs (request metadata, idempotency keys, status), and model usage logs (per-request tokens/metrics).
- Export options: logs can be streamed to customer-owned S3, pushed to syslog/HEC, or exported via daily/weekly log bundles. We also support structured JSON export for SIEM ingestion.
- Immutability: write-once storage for audit artifacts + signed export bundles are available for Dedicated/Private deployments; in hosted mode we maintain append-only event stores and tamper-evident hashes for exported bundles.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I’ll send the SOC 2 summary and an audit-logging one-pager (attached).
2) Dev (cc'd) will follow up with technical details on retention windows, field-level masking, and API log schemas.
3) If you can send the vendor security questionnaire (or a prioritized subset), we’ll start filling it out this week.

Do these next steps work for you? Happy to book a short follow-up with our security engineer if you prefer a live session.

Best,

Thanks John — great questions. I’ve attached a short one-pager that lists the API log schema at a high level; Dev will follow up with the full schema and retention options. Quick answers inline: 

1) Fields: we capture timestamp, request_id, caller_id (authenticated principal), endpoint, method, status_code, latency_ms, token_count, response_token_count, model_id, and a payload_hash. We do not persist full user prompt text by default in hosted mode unless the customer enables request logging for debugging; we can offer field-level masking or redaction.

2) Retention: hosted default 90 days for request logs, 1 year for admin audit trails; Dedicated can be configured up to customer-defined retention (multi-year) and Private deployments are customer-managed. For requests >1 year we can provide archive exports; discuss with legal for 7-year needs.

3) Export: yes — near-real-time streaming to cross-account S3 is supported via Kinesis or direct S3 PUTs; we also support scheduled daily bundles.

4) Immutability: for hosted exports we append events to an append-only store and provide a signed manifest containing SHA256 hashes for each daily bundle. For Dedicated/Private we can enable WORM-backed storage and HSM signing of bundles.

Aditya / Dev — can you provide the full API log schema and a brief note on masking controls? Also listing our suggested retention and export configs for Acme.

Marissa

Hi John — quick technical follow-up as promised. Below is a concise version of the API log schema and masking/export options. Happy to jump on a call to walk through samples.

API log schema (high-level fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id (UUID)
- caller_id (service or user id)
- session_id
- endpoint (e.g., /v1/generate)
- method (POST/GET)
- status_code
- latency_ms
- model_id
- token_count_in
- token_count_out
- payload_hash (SHA256)
- error_code (if any)
- custom_tags (customer-provided metadata)

Policy & masking options:
- Default: request/response payloads not stored. Metadata only + payload_hash.
- Optional: enable request logging with field-level redaction. You can mask prompt_text and any PII fields before storage.
- Export formats: JSONL for SIEM, compressed tar.gz bundles with signed manifest, or streaming via Kinesis/SQS to customer endpoint.

Retention & export configs we recommend for Acme: 
- Hosted: 90d request logs + 1y admin trails; daily signed export to S3 for archive.
- Dedicated: configure to 7y WORM archive for admin actions + 2y request logs, or push long-term to your Glacier tier.
- Private: fully customer-managed retention and storage.

Immutability details:
- Hosted signed manifests: each daily bundle contains file-level SHA256 and a signed manifest using Redwood's signing key. We provide the public cert for verification.
- For Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS/HSM to sign bundles on export.

Integration samples we can provide: CloudWatch/Splunk/Elastic ingestion snippets, S3 cross-account bucket policy template, and an example SIEM parsing rule. I’ll attach the templates in a follow-up message.

Regards,
